sanskrit: taṃ bhīmarūpaṃ tvaritaṃ dravantaṃ; duryodhanaṃ śatrusaho niṣaṅgī prākṣveḍayad yoddhumanāḥ kirīṭī; bāṇena viddhaṃ rudhiraṃ vamantam
english: Seeing that fearsome Duryodhana fleeing swiftly, the quiver-bearing Kirīṭī, eager to fight and enduring of enemies, roared a challenge at him — who had been pierced by an arrow and was vomiting blood.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca vihāya kīrtiṃ vipulaṃ yaśaś ca; yuddhāt parāvṛtya palāyase kim na te 'dya tūryāṇi samāhatāni; yathāvad udyānti gatasya yuddhe
english: Arjuna said: Abandoning your vast fame and glory, why do you flee, turning away from battle? Why do your war-drums not sound properly now as they did when you went to fight?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirasyāsmi nideśakārī; pārthas tṛtīyo yudhi ca sthiro 'smi tadartham āvṛtya mukhaṃ prayaccha; narendravṛttaṃ smara dhārtarāṣṭra
english: I act on Yudhiṣṭhira's command; I am Pārtha, the third, and I stand firm in battle. For his sake, turn your face and fight — remember the conduct of a king, O son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: moghaṃ tavedaṃ bhuvi nāmadheyaṃ; duryodhanetīha kṛtaṃ purastāt na hīha duryodhanatā tavāsti; palāyamānasya raṇaṃ vihāya
english: Your name in this world — 'Duryodhana,' given to you before — is rendered vain; for there is no quality of Duryodhana in you now, as you flee abandoning the battle.

sanskrit: na te purastād atha pṛṣṭhato vā; paśyāmi duryodhana rakṣitāram paraihi yuddhena kurupravīra; prāṇān priyān pāṇḍavato 'dya rakṣa
english: I see no protector of yours, neither in front nor behind you, O Duryodhana. Come, O foremost of the Kurus, protect your dear life from the Pāṇḍava through battle today.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca āhūyamānas tu sa tena saṃkhye; mahāmanā dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putraḥ nivartitas tasya girāṅkuśena; gajo yathā matta ivāṅkuśena
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Being thus summoned by him in battle, that great-souled son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra was turned back by his words as by a goad — like a maddened elephant turned by a goad.

sanskrit: so 'mṛṣyamāṇo vacasābhimṛṣṭo; mahārathenātirathas tarasvī paryāvavartātha rathena vīro; bhogī yathā pādatalābhimṛṣṭaḥ
english: Unable to endure being struck by those words of the great chariot-warrior, that swift hero, who surpassed all chariot-warriors, wheeled around in his chariot — like a serpent touched by the sole of a foot.

sanskrit: taṃ prekṣya karṇaḥ parivartamānaṃ; nivartya saṃstabhya ca viddhagātraḥ duryodhanaṃ dakṣiṇato 'bhyagacchat; pārthaṃ nṛvīro yudhi hemamālī
english: Seeing him turn back, Karṇa, though his body was pierced by arrows, steadied himself and turned back; that hero among men, wearing a garland of gold, came to Duryodhana's right flank to face Pārtha in battle.

sanskrit: bhīṣmas tataḥ śāṃtanavo nivṛtya; hiraṇyakakṣyāṃs tvarayaṃs turaṃgān duryodhanaṃ paścimato 'bhyarakṣat; pārthān mahābāhur adhijyadhanvā
english: Then Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, turning back and urging his gold-girthed horses, with his bow strung, the mighty-armed one guarded Duryodhana on the western flank from the sons of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: droṇaḥ kṛpaś caiva viviṃśatiś ca; duḥśāsanaś caiva nivṛtya śīghram sarve purastād vitateṣucāpā; duryodhanārthaṃ tvaritābhyupeyuḥ
english: Droṇa, Kṛpa, Viviṃśati, and Duḥśāsana — all of them quickly turned back, with their bows bent and arrows ready, and swiftly came to the front for the sake of Duryodhana.

sanskrit: sa tāny anīkāni nivartamānāny; ālokya pūrṇaughanibhāni pārthaḥ haṃso yathā megham ivāpatantaṃ; dhanaṃjayaḥ pratyapatat tarasvī
english: Seeing those armies turning back, resembling the fullness of flood-tide, Pārtha Dhanañjaya swiftly rushed toward them — as a swan flies toward an approaching cloud.

sanskrit: te sarvataḥ saṃparivārya pārtham; astrāṇi divyāni samādadānāḥ vavarṣur abhyetya śaraiḥ samantān; meghā yathā bhūdharam ambuvegaiḥ
english: They surrounded Pārtha from all sides, taking up their divine weapons, and advancing, showered him with arrows on every side — as clouds drench a mountain with torrents of water.

sanskrit: tato 'stram astreṇa nivārya teṣāṃ; gāṇḍīvadhanvā kurupuṃgavānām saṃmohanaṃ śatrusaho 'nyad astraṃ; prāduścakāraindrir apāraṇīyam
english: Then the wielder of Gāṇḍīva, bearing down the weapons of those foremost Kuru heroes with counter-weapons, the enemy-subduing son of Indra revealed another weapon — the irresistible Sammohana (bewildering) weapon.

sanskrit: tato diśaś cānudiśo vivṛtya; śaraiḥ sudhārair niśitaiḥ supuṅkhaiḥ gāṇḍīvaghoṣeṇa manāṃsi teṣāṃ; mahābalaḥ pravyathayāṃ cakāra
english: Then, turning in all the cardinal and intermediate directions, he of great strength, with well-edged, sharp, well-feathered arrows and by the roar of the Gāṇḍīva, caused terror to the minds of those warriors.

sanskrit: tataḥ punar bhīmaravaṃ pragṛhya; dorbhyāṃ mahāśaṅkham udāraghoṣam vyanādayat sa pradiśo diśaḥ khaṃ; bhuvaṃ ca pārtho dviṣatāṃ nihantā
english: Then, taking up his great conch of magnificent sound, the slayer of enemies Pārtha blew it mightily with his arms, and the sound filled all the cardinal and intermediate directions, the sky and the earth.

sanskrit: te śaṅkhanādena kurupravīrāḥ; saṃmohitāḥ pārthasamīritena utsṛjya cāpāni durāsadāni; sarve tadā śāntiparā babhūvuḥ
english: Those foremost Kuru heroes, bewildered by the blast of the conch blown by Pārtha, all let go of their formidable bows and became intent on peace at that moment.

sanskrit: tathā visaṃjñeṣu pareṣu pārthaḥ; smṛtvā tu vākyāni tathottarāyāḥ niryāhi madhyād iti matsyaputram; uvāca yāvat kuravo visaṃjñāḥ
english: While the enemies were thus rendered unconscious, Pārtha, remembering the words of Uttara, said to the son of Virāṭa: 'Drive out from among them, while the Kurus are still insensible.'

sanskrit: ācārya śāradvatayoḥ suśukle; karṇasya pītaṃ ruciraṃ ca vastram drauṇeś ca rājñaś ca tathaiva nīle; vastre samādatsva narapravīra
english: Fetch the two pure white garments of the teacher and of Śāradvata's son, the bright yellow garment of Karṇa, and likewise the dark blue garments of Droṇa's son and the king, O hero among men.

sanskrit: bhīṣmasya saṃjñāṃ tu tathaiva manye; jānāti me 'strapratighātam eṣaḥ etasya vāhān kuru savyatas tvam; evaṃ hi yātavyam amūḍhasaṃjñaiḥ
english: I think Bhīṣma has his senses — he knows how to counter my weapons. Keep his horses on the left side; that is how one must pass those who have not lost their senses.

sanskrit: raśmīn samutsṛjya tato mahātmā; rathād avaplutya virāṭaputraḥ vastrāṇy upādāya mahārathānāṃ; tūrṇaṃ punaḥ svaṃ ratham āruroha
english: Then the great-souled son of Virāṭa, releasing the reins, leapt down from the chariot, collected the garments of those great chariot-warriors, and quickly remounted his own chariot.

sanskrit: tato 'nvaśāsac caturaḥ sadaśvān; putro virāṭasya hiraṇyakakṣyān te tad vyatīyur dhvajinām anīkaṃ; śvetā vahanto 'rjunam ājimadhyāt
english: Then the son of Virāṭa guided the four excellent gold-girthed horses; the white steeds, bearing Arjuna, passed through the army of the banner-bearers and out from the midst of the battle.

sanskrit: tathā tu yāntaṃ puruṣapravīraṃ; bhīṣmaḥ śarair abhyahanat tarasvī sa cāpi bhīṣmasya hayān nihatya; vivyādha pārśve daśabhiḥ pṛṣatkaiḥ
english: As that foremost of men was thus moving away, the swift Bhīṣma struck him with arrows; and he in turn, having struck down Bhīṣma's horses, pierced him in the side with ten swift arrows.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno bhīṣmam apāsya yuddhe; viddhvāsya yantāram ariṣṭadhanvā tasthau vimukto rathavṛndamadhyād; rāhuṃ vidāryeva sahasraraśmiḥ
english: Then Arjuna, having set aside Bhīṣma in the battle and pierced his charioteer, with his bow intact, stood free from amid the multitude of chariots — as the thousand-rayed sun stands after rending Rāhu.

sanskrit: labdhvā tu saṃjñāṃ ca kurupravīraḥ; pārthaṃ samīkṣyātha mahendrakalpam raṇād vimuktaṃ sthitam ekam ājau; sa dhārtarāṣṭras tvarito babhāṣe
english: Having regained consciousness, that foremost of Kuru heroes, seeing Pārtha standing alone in the field, freed from the battle, equal to great Indra, that son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra spoke quickly.

sanskrit: ayaṃ kathaṃ svid bhavatāṃ vimuktas; taṃ vai prabadhnīta yathā na mucyet tam abravīc chāṃtanavaḥ prahasya; kva te gatā buddhir abhūt kva vīryam
english: He said: 'How has this one escaped from you? Capture him so he cannot get away!' To him Śaṃtanu's son laughed and said: 'Where has your intelligence gone? Where your valor?'

sanskrit: śāntiṃ parāśvasya yathā sthito 'bhūr; utsṛjya bāṇāṃś ca dhanuś ca citram na tv eva bībhatsur alaṃ nṛśaṃsaṃ; kartuṃ na pāpe 'sya mano niviṣṭam
english: You yourself stood at peace, breathing again, having let go of your arrows and your marvelous bow. But Bībhatsu is not capable of cruelty — his mind is not set on wickedness.

sanskrit: trailokyahetor na jahet svadharmaṃ; tasmān na sarve nihatā raṇe 'smin kṣipraṃ kurūn yāhi kurupravīra; vijitya gāś ca pratiyātu pārthaḥ
english: He would not abandon his own dharma even for the sake of the three worlds — that is why not all have been slain in this battle. Go quickly back to the Kuru lands, O foremost of Kurus; let Pārtha return, having won back the cattle.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tasya tu tan niśamya; pitāmahasyātmahitaṃ vaco 'tha atītakāmo yudhi so 'tyamarṣī; rājā viniḥśvasya babhūva tūṣṇīm
english: Hearing those words of the grandfather, which were truly for his own good, Duryodhana, the king, excessively wrathful and having lost the chance to win in battle, heaved a deep sigh and fell silent.

sanskrit: tad bhīṣmavākyaṃ hitam īkṣya sarve; dhanaṃjayāgniṃ ca vivardhamānam nivartanāyaiva mano nidadhyur; duryodhanaṃ te parirakṣamāṇāḥ
english: Seeing that beneficial speech of Bhīṣma, and the ever-growing fire of Dhanañjaya, all those who were protecting Duryodhana set their minds on retreating.

sanskrit: tān prasthitān prītamanāḥ sa pārtho; dhanaṃjayaḥ prekṣya kurupravīrān ābhāṣamāṇo 'nuyayau muhūrtaṃ; saṃpūjayaṃs tatra gurūn mahātmā
english: Seeing those foremost Kuru heroes setting out, Pārtha Dhanañjaya, with a gladdened mind, followed them for a moment, addressing them, and there that great-souled one honored his elders.

sanskrit: pitāmahaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ sa vṛddhaṃ; droṇaṃ guruṃ ca pratipūjya mūrdhnā drauṇiṃ kṛpaṃ caiva gurūṃś ca sarvāñ; śarair vicitrair abhivādya caiva
english: Honoring with bowed head the aged grandfather Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, the teacher Droṇa, and paying salutation with varied arrows to Droṇa's son, Kṛpa, and all his elders —

sanskrit: duryodhanasyottamaratnacitraṃ; ciccheda pārtho mukuṭaṃ śareṇa āmantrya vīrāṃś ca tathaiva mānyān; gāṇḍīvaghoṣeṇa vinādya lokān
english: — Pārtha cut off with an arrow the crown of Duryodhana, adorned with the finest jewels; and having taken leave of those heroes and venerable ones alike, and filling the worlds with the roar of the Gāṇḍīva —

sanskrit: sa devadattaṃ sahasā vinādya; vidārya vīro dviṣatāṃ manāṃsi dhvajena sarvān abhibhūya śatrūn; sa hemajālena virājamānaḥ
english: — that hero, suddenly blowing his Devadatta conch and splitting the hearts of his foes, having overpowered all enemies with his banner, shining with his net of gold —

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā prayātāṃs tu kurūn kirīṭī; hṛṣṭo 'bravīt tatra sa matsyaputram āvartayāśvān paśavo jitās te; yātāḥ pare yāhi puraṃ prahṛṣṭaḥ
english: — seeing the Kurus depart, the diademed Kirīṭī, overjoyed, said to the son of Matsya there: 'Turn the horses around — your cattle have been won. The enemies have gone. Go to your city rejoicing.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato vijitya saṃgrāme kurūn govṛṣabhekṣaṇaḥ samānayām āsa tadā virāṭasya dhanaṃ mahat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, having conquered the Kurus in battle, he whose eyes were like a bull's gathered together the great wealth of Virāṭa.

sanskrit: gateṣu ca prabhagneṣu dhārtarāṣṭreṣu sarvaśaḥ vanān niṣkramya gahanād bahavaḥ kurusainikāḥ
english: And when the forces of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son had all gone away, broken and dispersed in every direction, many of the Kuru soldiers emerged from the dense forest.

sanskrit: bhayāt saṃtrastamanasaḥ samājagmus tatas tataḥ muktakeśā vyadṛśyanta sthitāḥ prāñjalayas tadā
english: With minds terrified by fear they came from here and there; they appeared with unbound hair, standing with folded hands.

sanskrit: kṣutpipāsāpariśrāntā videśasthā vicetasaḥ ūcuḥ praṇamya saṃbhrāntāḥ pārtha kiṃ karavāma te
english: Exhausted by hunger and thirst, bewildered, in a foreign land and out of their senses, they bowed and said in confusion: 'O Pārtha, what shall we do for you?'

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca svasti vrajata bhadraṃ vo na bhetavyaṃ kathaṃ cana nāham ārtāñ jighāṃsāmi bhṛśaṃ āśvāsayāmi vaḥ
english: Arjuna said: 'Go in safety, good fortune be with you — you need not fear at all. I do not wish to slay the distressed. I greatly reassure you.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasya tām abhayāṃ vācaṃ śrutvā yodhāḥ samāgatāḥ āyuḥkīrtiyaśodābhis tam āśirbhir anandayan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing his words of assurance, the assembled warriors gladdened him with blessings of long life, fame, and glory.

sanskrit: tato nivṛttāḥ kuravaḥ prabhagnā vaśam āsthitāḥ panthānam upasaṃgamya phalguno vākyam abravīt
english: Then the Kurus, turned back and utterly routed, came under his sway; approaching the road, Phalguna spoke this word.

sanskrit: rājaputra pratyavekṣa samānītāni sarvaśaḥ gokulāni mahābāho vīra gopālakaiḥ saha
english: He said: 'O prince, O mighty-armed hero, review all the herds of cattle that have been rounded up together along with the cowherds.'

sanskrit: tato 'parāhṇe yāsyāmo virāṭanagaraṃ prati āśvāsya pāyayitvā ca pariplāvya ca vājinaḥ
english: Then in the afternoon we shall go toward the city of Virāṭa, after resting the horses, giving them water, and refreshing them.'

sanskrit: gacchantu tvaritāś caiva gopālāḥ preṣitās tvayā nagare priyam ākhyātuṃ ghoṣayantu ca te jayam
english: 'Let the cowherds whom you send go quickly to the city to announce the good news and proclaim your victory.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca uttaras tvaramāṇo 'tha dūtān ājñāpayat tataḥ vacanād arjunasyaiva ācakṣadhvaṃ jayaṃ mama
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Uttara, acting swiftly, commanded messengers accordingly, saying: 'Go and, by Arjuna's word, announce my victory.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca avajitya dhanaṃ cāpi virāṭo vāhinīpatiḥ prāviśan nagaraṃ hṛṣṭaś caturbhiḥ saha pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Virāṭa, the commander of the army, having also won back the wealth, entered the city rejoicing, together with the four Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: jitvā trigartān saṃgrāme gāś caivādāya kevalāḥ aśobhata mahārājaḥ saha pārthaiḥ śriyā vṛtaḥ
english: Having defeated the Trigartas in battle and recovered the cattle alone, the great king shone resplendent, accompanied by the sons of Pṛthā, enveloped in glory.

sanskrit: tam āsanagataṃ vīraṃ suhṛdāṃ prītivardhanam upatasthuḥ prakṛtayaḥ samastā brāhmaṇaiḥ saha
english: When that hero, who increased the joy of his friends, was seated upon his throne, all his ministers along with the brahmins attended upon him.

sanskrit: sabhājitaḥ sasainyas tu pratinandyātha matsyarāṭ visarjayām āsa tadā dvijāṃś ca prakṛtīs tathā
english: Honored and congratulated along with his army, the king of Matsya then dismissed the twice-born brahmins and the ministers.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā matsyānāṃ virāṭo vāhinīpatiḥ uttaraṃ paripapraccha kva yāta iti cābravīt
english: Then that king of the Matsyas, Virāṭa, the commander of the army, eagerly inquired about Uttara, saying: 'Where has he gone?'

sanskrit: ācakhyus tasya saṃhṛṣṭāḥ striyaḥ kanyāś ca veśmani antaḥpuracarāś caiva kurubhir godhanaṃ hṛtam
english: The women, maidens, and those who moved within the inner apartments joyfully told him at home that the cattle-wealth had been taken away by the Kurus.

sanskrit: vijetum abhisaṃrabdha eka evātisāhasāt bṛhannaḍāsahāyaś ca niryātaḥ pṛthivīṃjayaḥ
english: The conqueror of the earth had gone out alone, determined to win them back, with exceeding boldness, with Bṛhannaḍā as his companion.

sanskrit: upayātān atirathān droṇaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ kṛpam karṇaṃ duryodhanaṃ caiva droṇaputraṃ ca ṣaḍrathān
english: Six great chariot-warriors had come to oppose him: Droṇa, Śaṃtanu's son Bhīṣma, Kṛpa, Karṇa, Duryodhana, and Droṇa's son.

sanskrit: rājā virāṭo 'tha bhṛśaṃ prataptaḥ; śrutvā sutaṃ hy ekarathena yātam bṛhannaḍāsārathim ājivardhanaṃ; provāca sarvān atha mantrimukhyān
english: King Virāṭa, greatly distressed upon hearing that his son had gone with but one chariot, with Bṛhannaḍā as charioteer, he who increases victory in battle, then spoke to all the chief ministers.

sanskrit: sarvathā kuravas te hi ye cānye vasudhādhipāḥ trigartān nirjitāñ śrutvā na sthāsyanti kadā cana
english: The Kurus in particular, and whatever other lords of the earth, will certainly never stand idle upon hearing that the Trigartas have been defeated.

sanskrit: tasmād gacchantu me yodhā balena mahatā vṛtāḥ uttarasya parīpsārthaṃ ye trigartair avikṣatāḥ
english: Therefore let my warriors go, surrounded by a great force — those who were not wounded by the Trigartas — for the purpose of protecting Uttara.

sanskrit: hayāṃś ca nāgāṃś ca rathāṃś ca śīghraṃ; padātisaṃghāṃś ca tataḥ pravīrān prasthāpayām āsa sutasya hetor; vicitraśastrābharaṇopapannān
english: He quickly dispatched horses, elephants, chariots, and hosts of infantry — heroic warriors furnished with varied weapons and ornaments — for the sake of his son.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa rājā matsyānāṃ virāṭo 'kṣauhiṇīpatiḥ vyādideśātha tāṃ kṣipraṃ vāhinīṃ caturaṅgiṇīm
english: Thus that king of the Matsyas, Virāṭa, the lord of an akshauhini, commanded that fourfold army to march out swiftly.

sanskrit: kumāram āśu jānīta yadi jīvati vā na vā yasya yantā gataḥ ṣaṇḍho manye 'haṃ na sa jīvati
english: He said: 'Find the prince quickly — whether he lives or not. A eunuch went as his charioteer; I think he cannot be alive.'

sanskrit: tam abravīd dharmarājaḥ prahasya; virāṭam ārtaṃ kurubhiḥ prataptam bṛhannaḍā sārathiś cen narendra; pare na neṣyanti tavādya gās tāḥ
english: The Dharma-king laughed and said to Virāṭa, afflicted and distressed by the Kurus: 'O lord of men, if Bṛhannaḍā is the charioteer, your enemies will not carry off those cattle today.'

sanskrit: sarvān mahīpān sahitān kurūṃś ca; tathaiva devāsurayakṣanāgān alaṃ vijetuṃ samare sutas te; svanuṣṭhitaḥ sārathinā hi tena
english: 'Your son is fully capable of conquering in battle all the kings together with the Kurus, and likewise the gods, demons, yakshas, and nagas — guided well by that charioteer.'

sanskrit: athottareṇa prahitā dūtās te śīghragāminaḥ virāṭanagaraṃ prāpya jayam āvedayaṃs tadā
english: Then those swift-moving messengers sent by Uttara reached the city of Virāṭa and announced the victory.

sanskrit: rājñas tataḥ samācakhyau mantrī vijayam uttamam parājayaṃ kurūṇāṃ cāpy upāyāntaṃ tathottaram
english: The minister then reported to the king the supreme victory, the defeat of the Kurus, and Uttara's return.

sanskrit: sarvā vinirjitā gāvaḥ kuravaś ca parājitāḥ uttaraḥ saha sūtena kuśalī ca paraṃtapa
english: 'All the cattle have been fully won back, the Kurus have been defeated, and Uttara is safe along with his charioteer, O scorcher of enemies.'

sanskrit: kaṅka uvāca diṣṭyā te nirjitā gāvaḥ kuravaś ca parājitāḥ diṣṭyā te jīvitaḥ putraḥ śrūyate pārthivarṣabha
english: Kaṅka said: 'By good fortune your cattle have been won back and the Kurus defeated. By good fortune your son is heard to be alive, O bull among kings.'

sanskrit: nādbhutaṃ tv eva manye 'haṃ yat te putro 'jayat kurūn dhruva eva jayas tasya yasya yantā bṛhannaḍā
english: 'I do not consider it a wonder that your son conquered the Kurus — certain indeed is the victory of one whose charioteer is Bṛhannaḍā.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato virāṭo nṛpatiḥ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ śrutvā tu vijayaṃ tasya kumārasyāmitaujasaḥ ācchādayitvā dūtāṃs tān mantriṇaḥ so 'bhyacodayat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then King Virāṭa, his body hair thrilling with delight upon hearing the victory of that prince of boundless energy, rewarded those messengers with garments and urged his ministers on.

sanskrit: rājamārgāḥ kriyantāṃ me patākābhir alaṃkṛtāḥ puṣpopahārair arcyantāṃ devatāś cāpi sarvaśaḥ
english: 'Let my royal roads be decorated with banners; let the gods be worshipped everywhere with floral offerings.'

sanskrit: kumārā yodhamukhyāś ca gaṇikāś ca svalaṃkṛtāḥ vāditrāṇi ca sarvāṇi pratyudyāntu sutaṃ mama
english: 'Let the princes, chief warriors, and courtesans, all well adorned, and all the musical instruments go forth to meet my son.'

sanskrit: ghaṇṭāpaṇavakaḥ śīghraṃ mattam āruhya vāraṇam śṛṅgāṭakeṣu sarveṣu ākhyātu vijayaṃ mama
english: 'Let the drummer quickly mount a maddened elephant and proclaim my victory at every crossroads.'

sanskrit: uttarā ca kumārībhir bahvībhir abhisaṃvṛtā śṛṅgāraveṣābharaṇā pratyudyātu bṛhannaḍām
english: 'And let Uttara, accompanied by many maidens, adorned in fine dress and ornaments, go forth to meet Bṛhannaḍā.'

sanskrit: śrutvā tu tad vacanaṃ pārthivasya; sarve punaḥ svastikapāṇayaś ca bheryaś ca tūryāṇi ca vārijāś ca; veṣaiḥ parārdhyaiḥ pramadāḥ śubhāś ca
english: Hearing the king's command, all with auspicious articles in hand, together with kettledrums, musical instruments, conches, and auspicious women beautifully attired in the finest garments —

sanskrit: tathaiva sūtāḥ saha māgadhaiś ca; nandīvādyāḥ paṇavās tūryavādyāḥ purād virāṭasya mahābalasya; pratyudyayuḥ putram anantavīryam
english: — and likewise bards along with panegyrists, players of the nandi drum, players of the paṇava and other instruments, went forth from the city of mighty Virāṭa to meet the son of boundless valor.

sanskrit: prasthāpya senāṃ kanyāś ca gaṇikāś ca svalaṃkṛtāḥ matsyarājo mahāprājñaḥ prahṛṣṭa idam abravīt akṣān āhara sairandhri kaṅka dyūtaṃ pravartatām
english: Having dispatched the army and the maidens and courtesans, all well adorned, the highly wise king of Matsya, overjoyed, said: 'Fetch the dice, Sairandhrī; let gambling begin, Kaṅka.'

sanskrit: taṃ tathā vādinaṃ dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavaḥ pratyabhāṣata na devitavyaṃ hṛṣṭena kitaveneti naḥ śrutam
english: Seeing him speak thus, the Pāṇḍava replied: 'We have heard it said that a gambler elated with joy should not gamble.'

sanskrit: na tvām adya mudā yuktam ahaṃ devitum utsahe priyaṃ tu te cikīrṣāmi vartatāṃ yadi manyase
english: 'I am not willing to gamble with you today when you are filled with joy; but I wish to do what is pleasing to you — let it proceed if you think it right.'

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca striyo gāvo hiraṇyaṃ ca yac cānyad vasu kiṃ cana na me kiṃ cit tvayā rakṣyam antareṇāpi devitum
english: Virāṭa said: 'Women, cattle, gold, and whatever other wealth there may be — nothing of mine is to be withheld by you; you may gamble without restraint.'

sanskrit: kaṅka uvāca kiṃ te dyūtena rājendra bahudoṣeṇa mānada devane bahavo doṣās tasmāt tat parivarjayet
english: Kaṅka said: 'What use is gambling to you, O lord of kings, O granter of honor? Gambling has many faults; therefore one should avoid it.'

sanskrit: śrutas te yadi vā dṛṣṭaḥ pāṇḍavo vai yudhiṣṭhiraḥ sa rājyaṃ sumahat sphītaṃ bhrātṝṃś ca tridaśopamān
english: 'Have you heard of, or perhaps seen, the Pāṇḍava Yudhiṣṭhira? He, his great and flourishing kingdom, and his brothers equal to the thirty gods —'

sanskrit: dyūte hāritavān sarvaṃ tasmād dyūtaṃ na rocaye atha vā manyase rājan dīvyāva yadi rocate
english: '— all were lost in gambling. Therefore I do not favor gambling. Or if you think otherwise, O king, let us gamble if it pleases you.'
